subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)

Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)

Hi Julia -

Thanks again for the time today - really helpful to hear how Globex is thinking about multilingual product search and CS routing across EU and APAC locales. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we all have the same plan.

Recap from today's call:
- Primary objectives: improve French/German search relevance in EU, and Japanese/Korean intent classification in APAC.
- Key signals: relevance (precision@1), hallucination risk on product descriptions, token-cost sensitivity for high QPS endpoints.
- Data constraints: GDPR-sensitive PII in EU logs; you prefer a Private deployment for evaluation but are open to a Hosted sandbox for initial tests.

Recommended short list of models to evaluate (initial):
1) redwood-mt-1.0 (multilingual foundation) - strong cross-lingual performance, good baseline for intent/classification.
2) redwood-translate-xl (locale-aware variant) - better for generation/rewrites in EU languages.
3) redwood-qa-compact (quantized) - cost efficient for high-throughput classification; watch for small regressions on edge cases.

Files I attached for initial evals:
- prompt-set-globex-v1.csv - curated prompt sets for FR/DE/JA/KO (you can add more rows).
- benchmark-results-20260212.pdf - internal benchmark snapshot on similar retail workload (latency & quality).

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share a small sample of your utterances (10-20 per locale) and any failing examples (you mentioned a sheet).
2) We spin up a 2-week eval: host model endpoints in EU region (Private if you prefer) and run the prompt set + live sampling.
3) Rishi will run locale-specific quality checks and produce a pass/fail matrix and recommended prompt tweaks.
4) Quick sync next Wed to review preliminary metrics and agree on broader rollout.

Can you confirm timelines for sharing the sample utterances and whether you'd like Private evals from day 1?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications from my side:

1) Languages / priority: FR and DE are top for us in EU (70% of traffic), then NL and ES; in APAC we need JA and KO first, then ZH-HK later.
2) Hallucinations: we see frequent product-description hallucination when generative rewrites run on sparse SKUs - can Redwood quantify/regress those cases?
3) Data: we can share a sanitized sample sheet (attached) with 15 utterances per locale and a small set of failing examples.

We attached globex-sample-utterances.xlsx - please let me know if the format works. On Private vs Hosted: we prefer Private for EU evals due to GDPR, but if you can do an initial smoke test on Hosted in eu-west-1 that would speed things up.

Can we aim for the 2-week eval starting Feb 23? If that works, Anil and I will confirm the sanitized sample by EOD next Monday.

Best,
Julia
Director, Search & Personalization
Globex Retail

Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)

Hi Julia -

Thanks for the sample and the questions. A couple technical notes and what we'll deliver during the 2-week eval:

Technical notes:
- Model tradeoffs: redwood-mt-1.0 will give the best out-of-the-box intent/classification across FR/DE/JA/KO. For generative rewrites (product descriptions), redwood-translate-xl or a fine-tuned variant reduces hallucination by ~15-20% in our benchmarks, at modest cost increase.
- Quantization: redwood-qa-compact (8-bit) is a good cost/latency tradeoff for classification. We'll validate no quality regression on your failing examples; if we see regressions we'll recommend the 16-bit variant for those routes.
- Privacy: for Private evals we can provide a temporary VPC-connected Private control plane with RBAC limited to Globex evaluators; you'll retain audit logs.

Deliverables for the eval (what we'll produce):
1) Locale-specific quality dashboard (precision@1, recall, hallucination incidents) per prompt set.
2) Per-model latency & cost breakdown (token cost, avg RT).
3) Suggested prompt-set tweaks and a small set of instruction-following prompts for FR/DE/JA/KO.
4) Regression report with counterexamples and suggested mitigation (prompt edits, fallback routing to larger model).

Operational ask from Globex:
- Please confirm whether you want the Private eval in eu-west-1 from day one or if a Hosted smoke test first is acceptable.
- We need the sanitized sample sheet (15 per locale) and any blacklisted terms to avoid in prompts.

I'll coordinate with Priyom to provision the eval infra and will share a folder with initial runs.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
